articles.headline: MCL sprain sidelines Mariota; Daniels preps for full practice
articles.description: In his team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL of his right knee, and the timetable for his return remains uncertain coach Dan Quinn said on Monday.
articles.headlineJa: マリオタがMCL捻挫で離脱、ダニエルズはフル練習に向け準備
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のインディアナポリス・コルツ戦で敗れたワシントン・コマンダーズのクォーターバック、マーカス・マリオタが右膝の内側側副靭帯（MCL）を捻挫した。ダン・クイン監督は月曜日、復帰時期は依然として不透明であると述べた。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL of his right knee, but the timetable for his return remains uncertain, coach Dan Quinn said Monday.

Quinn also reiterated that starting quarterback Jayden Daniels will practice in full this week, with the hope of starting Sunday against the visiting New York Giants.

Mariota had started the past two games in place of Daniels, who was sidelined with a dislocated left elbow.

Daniels has played a full game just five times since the start of the 2025 season, adding to Mariota's importance.

But after leading the Commanders to a 33-31 home win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, Mariota suffered the same injury on Sunday that occurred in an Aug. 14 preseason game versus the Miami Dolphins. He was able to return to practice on Sept. 1 following August's setback.

Mariota led field goal drives on his only two series Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts for a 6-0 lead; the Commanders (1-3) would go on to lose 30-13 in London. Mariota was sacked by defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore on third-and-goal from the 6-yard line, causing the signal-caller's right knee to bend.

Rookie seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis relieved Mariota, completing 15-of-33 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown with one interception in his first NFL action.

Quinn said the Commanders want to see how Mariota progresses before deciding whether they need to add another quarterback.

Washington will play at the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 19 before its bye week.

Mariota started eight games last season, and he has played in 17 overall since signing with Washington in 2024.  He has thrown 18 touchdowns and seven interceptions in those contests.

Washington also lost its punt and kick returner Jaylin Lane to a fractured and dislocated ankle, ending his season. Lane averaged 13.7 yards per punt return with two touchdowns last season. He had been averaging 12.0 yards this campaign as well as 24.6 yards on kick returns. The injury occurred on a kick return Sunday.

Quinn indicated that, in addition to Daniels, the Commanders are hopeful two other starters will return: safety Nick Cross (internal injury) and right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion). Running back Rachaad White (shoulder) also might be back.

Quinn said they're not yet sure what Terry McLaurin will do in practice this week. The wide receiver missed Sunday's loss to the Colts after injuring a hamstring in Friday's practice.

articles.headline: Ex-Bears LB Wilson in altercation with security at Soldier Field
articles.description: Former Bears Super Bowl champion linebacker Otis Wilson was involved in an altercation with a female and male security officer at Soldier Field on Sunday after a dispute about elevator usage.
articles.headlineJa: 元ベアーズLBウィルソン氏、ソルジャー・フィールドで警備員と衝突
articles.descriptionJa: 元ベアーズでスーパーボウル制覇を経験したラインバッカーのオーティス・ウィルソン氏が日曜、ソルジャー・フィールドにてエレベーターの利用を巡る争いの末、男女の警備員と揉み合いになった。
articles.body:
Former Bears Super Bowl-champion linebacker Otis Wilson was involved in an altercation with a female and male security officer at Soldier Field on Sunday after a dispute about elevator usage at the conclusion of Chicago's game against the Jets.

In response to a question from ESPN about the incident with Wilson, Monterrey Security, the company contracted by Soldier Field to provide security on Bears gamedays, said that Wilson was not wearing credentials, and after a female officer "politely" directed him to use a different elevator bank, he "forced his way" onto the elevator and then became "physically combative and violently attacked" the female officer. "He aggressively threw the female officer into a wall," the statement said, "leaving a large hole in the wall."

In a statement to ESPN, Wilson said he and his wife entered an elevator with media personnel to leave Soldier Field and were both "assaulted by private security personnel."

"Before being able to identify myself as a former Chicago Bears player and attempt to explain why we were there," Wilson said in the statement, "a security guard approached us and the guard physically assaulted my wife."

Wilson said he was then also assaulted by the two security contractors and was then transported by ambulance to Northwestern Memorial Hospital for evaluation and released that night.

Per Monterrey Security, the female officer, a 5-foot-4 off-duty law enforcement officer who has worked at Soldier Field since 2024, was transported to a hospital for treatment of her injuries, "which include substantial bruising and injuries to her ribs and arms."

The Chicago Police Department confirmed to ESPN that officers responded to Northwestern Memorial Hospital to take a report for the incident that occurred at Soldier Field, and there is an active investigation.

Both Wilson and Monterrey Security said they will cooperate with law enforcement and any official review.

Multiple reporters, including from ESPN, witnessed the moments that preceded the altercation. Wilson, 69, and his wife Tina boarded an elevator on suite level A, near the press box. The elevator was intended for media use only and contained credentialed reporters when Wilson and his wife were the last to enter. A female security officer employed by Monterrey Security asked Wilson and his wife to get off the elevator because it was reserved for media use only. Wilson did not respond to her request. She asked him again to leave the elevator and then told him that the elevator would not be moving until he got off. Wilson said, "OK then" and did not move. A reporter on the elevator said, "Come on, we have a job to do."

The female security officer then got onto the elevator to physically pull Tina Wilson and then Otis Wilson off the elevator. Tina Wilson walked off the elevator and a male security officer then came to help the female officer remove Wilson from the elevator. articles.description: Veteran running back Joe Mixon is signing with the Seahawks, but is the 30-year-old worth adding in fantasy?
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボールの話題：ジョー・ミックスンはシアトル加入後、獲得する価値があるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ベテランRBのジョー・ミックスンがシーホークスと契約することになったが、この30歳の選手をファンタジー・チームに加える価値はあるだろうか？
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 5: Is Joe Mixon worth picking up after Seattle signing?

By Michael F. Florio

Joe Mixon is signing with the Seahawks, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

We have not seen Mixon since the 2024 season when he was with Houston. That season, he posted 1,325 scrimmage yards and 12 touchdowns. That was his fourth straight season topping 1,250 yards and scoring at least nine touchdowns.

Mixon, now 30, is returning from a foot injury that cost him the 2025 season. While there is reason to be skeptical Mixon could reach his old level, he is still a big name that has a productive history in the NFL, signing with a team that needs healthy running backs. That creates value in fantasy football.

While he is not a top target, Mixon is worth adding off the waiver wire this week, just to see what he has left. It's not a bad idea trying to trade him if you are able to add him off the waiver wire. People tend to love a big name.

At least for the time being, the Seahawks should still be led by Emanuel Wilson, who just went for 120 yards and two scores Sunday. He will be one of the top waiver wire adds this week in leagues he is still available. The Seahawks have activated Zach Charbonnet's practice window last week, giving them 21 days to activate him. They have already ruled him out for Week 5. Jadarian Price, who is on IR with a chest injury, is out at least three more games.

Oct. 5: Who did -- or didn't -- get the ball on Sunday?

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

By Eric Moody

Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders

Rachaad White's shoulder injury gave Jacory Croskey-Merritt a chance to take control of the backfield, but that didn't happen. He finished with 11 touches for 50 total yards and 7.0 fantasy points. Austin Ekeler got more involved as the game went on, finishing with five touches for 40 yards and 5.0 points while splitting early-down snaps with Croskey-Merritt in the second half. Ekeler is worth adding in deeper leagues, while Croskey-Merritt is tougher to trust. Kaytron Allen had just three touches for one yard, with Ekeler and Craig Reynolds both playing ahead of him.

New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills

James Cook III finished with 14 touches and 16.3 fantasy points against the Patriots, but it's worth noting that he set a season-low snap total. articles.headline: NFL Week 4: CeeDee Lamb, Joe Burrow and more fuel best quotes
articles.description: From family reunions to postgame trash talk, here are some of the sharpest sound bites and one-liners from around the league in Week 4.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第4週：シーディー・ラムやジョー・バロウらが放った今週の名言集
articles.descriptionJa: 家族との再会から試合後のトラッシュトークまで、リーグ各所で飛び出した第4週の鋭いコメントや名フレーズをまとめました。
articles.body:
Week 4 in the NFL wasn't short on entertainment.

Before "Monday Night Football" between the Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints, the week featured 10 games decided by one score. 

The close finishes provided plenty of fuel for trash talk and sharp sound bites as some of the game's best moments come from what's said before or after the whistle.

Players and coaches carried their teams' momentum from the field to the podium, delivering standout lines in their postgame sessions.

From bold statements to perfectly timed one-liners, here are the best quotes from around the NFL in Week 4.

"My grandma came out here, which was really good to see."

Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb

Delivering a dominant performance in his adopted hometown, Lamb guided the Cowboys to a dramatic triumph Sunday afternoon.

The wideout had a career-high 17 receptions for 189 yards, capped by a go-ahead 12-yard touchdown grab with under a minute remaining to seal a 34-30 decision over the winless Texans.

Originally from Louisiana, Lamb relocated to the Houston region following Hurricane Katrina in 2005. A large contingent of family members, including his grandmother, traveled to watch Lamb on Sunday.

"Obviously, we had our opportunities in the last two weeks, but this isn't Armageddon or anything."

Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow

Addressing his team's consecutive defeats following a 2-0 opening stretch, Burrow openly acknowledged his frustration while maintaining perspective on Cincinnati's outlook.

"You can't ride the roller coaster week-to-week," Burrow added. "You're going to win some; you're going to lose some. Obviously, you want to win every single one [and] you're going to fight like hell to make it happen, but we're not going to ride that roller coaster."

"We're not going to get into any bulletin board material. ... An elevated guy made a hell of a catch -- probably won't hear from him again. ... A practice squad player made a hell of a play."

Buffalo Bills CB C.J. Gardner-Johnson

Wide receiver Efton Chism III hauled in a sensational one-handed touchdown reception Sunday, sealing the Patriots' 29-26 comeback victory over the Bills. The play marked just the seventh career reception for Chism, an undrafted free agent in 2025 who, Gardner-Johnson's quip notwithstanding, has spent his entire tenure on the active roster rather than the practice squad. After signing with New England as an undrafted rookie in 2025, Chism secured a place on the 53-man roster out of training camp. Across 11 regular-season appearances in his young career, the receiver has remained on the main squad without ever being relegated to practice team status.

After the game, Gardner-Johnson downplayed the clutch moment. 

"For a guy that has been on eight teams in four years, I mean, I guess he knows the drill."

New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel

articles.headline: NFL Week 4's best arrivals, led by Saints DE Cam Jordan
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第4週のベスト・アライバル：セインツのDEカム・ジョーダンがトップに
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日の会場入りを毎週のファッション・ショーへと変え続けている。
articles.body:
Week 4 of the NFL season has arrived, and the calendar has officially flipped to October. But sweater weather hasn't quite followed everywhere. 

Unseasonable heat out West could keep layers light for another week, while cooler temperatures settling in across the East are opening the door for more fall-ready fits. That means players have plenty of options as they make their Week 4 entrances. With three weeks of looks already in the books, personal styles are also starting to take shape around the league. Some players have leaned into statement pieces, while others have kept things clean and understated.

From warm-weather looks to seasonal layers, Week 4 brings another round of game-day style as the calendar officially turns to fall.

Monday night drip

New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan opted for Saints colors in his look before "Monday Night Football." He rocked a gold and black checkered jacket and black pants on arrival. His quarterback, Tyler Shough, paid homage to the annual Bayou Classic held at Caesars Superdome with a clean shirt. Meanwhile, Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. wore an all-black fit with a gold chain necklace.

Primetime fashion

Ahead of the Detroit Lions and Carolina Panthers tilt on "Sunday Night Football," Aidan Hutchinson donned a fuzzy color-block sweater vest with black jeans and boots. And, of course, he had his signature gallon water jug in hand. 
Sunday style

The best design is in the details. Super Bowl champion Uchenna Nwosu and his celebrity stylist Ini Ikpe prioritize weekly custom game-day looks from Black and Brown designers.

This week, Ikpe took us inside the Abasi x Jagne denim fit Nwosu is displaying this Sunday -- a partnership with Baba Jagne, a Senegalese Gambian designer based in Los Angeles who is known for silhouettes and patterns that make you look twice.

"It's a cropped jacket and wide-leg trousers in dark indigo raw denim with copper contrast stitching. The jacket takes the classic trucker and rebuilds it," Ikpe said. "Its front panels snap on and off so they can be rearranged, which leaves an open U-shaped cutout down the front. Panels curve around the body, a buckled strap sits at the hem, and the sleeves sweep down from the shoulder. The trousers have a tan leather belt that dips and curves down the front, darted knees and a long, flared leg. Cognac leather JAGNE patches finish both pieces."

Nwosu's favorite part is that nobody else has this look; he's the first to wear it and feels unapologetically authentic to his style.

It's a small glimpse into just how much attention some of the best-dressed NFL players, like Nwosu, put into their game-day tunnel fit. -- Cameron Wolfe 

Sunday's Best

Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai arrived in a custom matching jacket gifted to him by Brenda, a Bears fan and breast cancer patient at Advocate Health Care.

articles.headline: Sources: Clippers' Max Strus (foot) out at least 4 weeks
articles.description: Clippers wing Max Strus suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his right foot and will be reevaluated in four weeks, league sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：クリッパーズのマックス・ストラス（足）が少なくとも4週間離脱
articles.descriptionJa: クリッパーズのウィング、マックス・ストラスが右足の足底筋膜を部分的に断裂し、4週間後に再評価を受けることがリーグ関係者からESPNに伝えられた。
articles.body:
LA Clippers wing Max Strus suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his right foot during Sunday's preseason opener in Hawaii and will be reevaluated in four weeks, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

It was a non-contact injury five minutes into the game. Strus cut across the lane to receive a pass and, as he caught it, pulled up lame and struggled to put weight on his right foot.

 

Clippers coach Ty Lue called timeout immediately and Strus limped slowly to the locker room, knowing something was wrong. Tests in Los Angeles after the flight back from Honolulu confirmed the partial plantar fascia tear.

This is the latest injury blow for an already shorthanded Clippers team. Brandon Ingram, acquired from the Toronto Raptors in the Kawhi Leonard trade and expected to be one of the Clippers' leading scorers, is still recovering from heel surgery and a partially torn Achilles that was repaired in May.

Ingram has only recently advanced to light court work and will miss the start of the season. Veteran guard Bradley Beal (right knee inflammation) and second-year center Yanic Konan Niederhauser (foot) are also currently out.

The Clippers open the regular season on Oct. 21 against the Sacramento Kings.

Oct. 5

Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting extension soon

New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday that, "It don't look good" in regards to him and the franchise agreeing to a contract extension before the start of the season.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million.

Oct. 2

Hawkins, Grizzlies mutually agree to part ways

The Memphis Grizzlies and guard Jordan Hawkins have agreed to part ways via waivers, allowing the 2023 lottery pick to find a new home in free agency, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The move comes three weeks after arriving as part of a four-player trade with the New Orleans Pelicans for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

articles.body:
Former lottery pick Jordan Hawkins is signing a two-way deal with the Chicago Bulls, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Hawkins was waived by the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday, three weeks after he arrived as part of a four-player trade with the New Orleans Pelicans for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

Hawkins was drafted with the 14th pick by the Pelicans in the 2023 draft. He appeared in 51 games last season for New Orleans but struggled to find consistent playing time. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

articles.headline: NBA testing smart basketballs, wrist wearables in preseason
articles.description: The NBA is experimenting with smart basketballs and wrist wearables for officials in select preseason games in order to collect data on the review process.
articles.headlineJa: NBA、プレシーズンでスマートボールとリストバンド型ウェアラブルを試験導入
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは、ビデオ判定プロセスに関するデータを収集するため、一部のプレシーズンゲームにおいて、スマートボールと審判用のリストバンド型ウェアラブルを試験的に導入している。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The NBA is experimenting with two pieces of technology in the leadup to the season, the league announced Monday.

Select exhibition games will include a smart basketball that has a Bluetooth sensor in it and can collect data for future use in real-time officiating decisions. The league said the information from the Wilson-developed "connected" balls will be for research only and not affect calls made during those games.

Officials in select games will also use wrist wearables to communicate with the replay center in designated situations, including replay reviews, scoring changes and clock malfunctions.

The wearables went through what the NBA called a successful pilot program during the summer league. The technology will not extend into the regular season.

articles.headline: Hornets guard Coby White to sit preseason after calf strain
articles.description: Hornets guard Coby White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the remainder of preseason, the team announced Monday.
articles.headlineJa: ホーネッツのガード、コービー・ホワイトがふくらはぎの筋挫傷によりプレシーズン欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ホーネッツは月曜日、ガードのコービー・ホワイトがトレーニングキャンプ中に左ふくらはぎの筋挫傷を負い、プレシーズンの残りの試合を欠場することを発表した。
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets guard Coby White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the remainder of preseason, the team announced Monday.

White, 26, signed a three-year, $74 million contract with Charlotte over the summer and is expected to play a large role this season after the LaMelo Ball trade left a void in the backcourt.

White joins second-year guard Kon Knueppel on the sideline for the remainder of preseason. Knueppel suffered a left hamstring strain earlier in training camp.

The Hornets acquired White from the Chicago Bulls in February and he went on to have a strong finish to the season with his new team. He was the hero in the team's play-in victory over the Miami Heat, scoring 19 points and hitting the turnaround 3 late in regulation to force overtime.

The Hornets' preseason begins Tuesday night while their regular season opens on the road in Brooklyn on October 21.

articles.headline: How the sportsbooks adjust after high volume of early-season NFL injuries
articles.description: With several players out for an extended time (some for the entire season), sportsbooks have reacted quickly.
articles.headlineJa: NFLシーズン序盤に怪我が多発し、ブックメーカーはどう対応しているのか
articles.descriptionJa: 複数の選手が長期離脱（中にはシーズン全休となる選手も）したことを受け、ブックメーカーは迅速に対応しています。
articles.body:
Injuries play a key role in the (mis)fortunes of every team over the course of the NFL season. Nearly a quarter of the way through the 2026 campaign, the list of star players facing significant injuries is staggering, leaving bettors and bookmakers alike scrambling to adjust.

Quarterbacks play the most important position in the game and are, naturally, perennial favorites for Most Valuable Player. Thus far, five quarterbacks who began the season as starters have sustained serious injuries: Jayden Daniels, Lamar Jackson, Baker Mayfield, Caleb Williams and Jaxson Dart (who is out for the season). 

A sampling of names from other offensive skill positions include Saquon Barkley, Travis Etienne Jr., A.J. Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson, DeVonta Smith and De'Von Achane (who is also out for the season). There have been several big names to go down on the defensive side of the ball as well, though those generally have less impact for betting purposes.

Individual games are usually a starting point for sportsbooks when adjusting for injuries. Every player has a value that plays into any given game's line, so when an injury occurs -- whether before a game or during it -- sportsbooks take into account how many points to the spread that player is worth. 

For example, the Chicago Bears opened as 1.5-point home favorites in lookahead lines for their Week 3 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, but when Williams sustained his hamstring injury in Week 2, the line ultimately moved to Bears +4.5, a five-point swing based essentially on one player.

That said, sportsbooks can sometimes overrate a player's importance or underrate a team's resilience in those situations: The Bears are 2-0 straight up and against the spread with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent under center.

"One of the biggest lessons from this season has been that we've probably undervalued the backups," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Time and time again, reserve quarterbacks and 'next men up' have stepped in and performed above expectations, and the book has found itself on the wrong side of more than a few of those results."

Feazel says that a star player leaving a game injured means the sportsbook has to adjust its numbers "immediately." The Baltimore Ravens, for example, ended up not covering their pregame line of -11.5 after Jackson left injured against the Tennessee Titans, meaning a confident bettor could have gotten nice value on the Titans spread in the second half, when the Ravens offense scored zero points.

Most of the major sportsbooks also now offer some form of injury insurance -- a more popular feature in recent seasons -- that refunds player props should a player leave hurt. However, it often only covers the first half unless bettors pay a premium to cover the whole game.

Looking towards futures, a major injury will have an obvious effect on the given player's season statistical props, as well as their odds to win awards.

Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. - Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

articles.headline: Jordan Pickford ignored give-way sign, almost caused crash, court hears
articles.description: England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.
articles.headlineJa: ジョーダン・ピックフォード、譲れの標識を無視し衝突寸前、法廷で明らかに
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドのゴールキーパー、ジョーダン・ピックフォードが、20万ポンドのスーパーカー、ランボルギーニを不注意に運転し、他の2台の車との衝突事故を引き起こしかけたことが法廷で明らかにされた。
articles.body:
England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.

The 32-year-old was pulled over by police after ignoring a give-way sign, forcing two cars to slam on the brakes, and then speeding off into the distance.

The incident happened in the upmarket Cheshire town of Knutsford on April 14, sparking a criminal prosecution for driving without due care or attention.

Pickford, who has 336 appearances for Everton and 92 England caps, has pleaded guilty to the charge and requested a court hearing to explain his mitigation.

According to court documents, Pc Cecil Ricardo, from Cheshire Police, said he had just left the station when he saw Pickford's blue Lamborghini Urus complete with personalised number plates.

"I was stationary on Bexton Road, Knutsford, waiting for traffic signals to turn green," he wrote.

"I then witnessed a blue Lamborghini Urus driving along Princess Street.

"It reached the junction with Toft Road, completely ignored the give way lines and pulled onto Toft Road causing two vehicles to slam on their brakes to avoid a collision.

"The Lamborghini then sped down Toft Road, Knutsford."

Pc Ricardo said he activated his lights and siren to set off in pursuit of the Lamborghini, noticing he was driving at 50mph while the Lamborghini "was still pulling away." 

"The speed limit on that stretch of Toft Road, Knutsford, is 30mph," he noted.

The officer said Pickford appeared to notice the chasing police car and pulled over.

Pickford pleaded guilty in writing in the Single Justice Procedure and told Warrington Magistrates Court: "I would like to attend court to put forward my mitigation."

His case was formally adjourned last week until a hearing at Chester Magistrates' Court on Dec. 7.

Pickford, who started his career at Sunderland before loan spells at six clubs including Burton, Bradford and Preston, has featured for England at the 2018, 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and was in goal for the country's Euro 2020 and 2024 final appearances.

articles.headline: JJ Gabriel representatives demanded game time at Manchester United - sources
articles.description: Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人がマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの出場時間を要求 - 関係者談
articles.descriptionJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人が、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドとの奨学金契約に関する交渉を開始する前に、サバFK、ブライトン、ボーンマス戦で少なくとも20分間の出場を要求したと、関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.

Gabriel, 15, has not trained with United since walking out on the club ahead of their Carabao Cup tie with Brighton on Sept. 16.

He is pictured in United's squad photo, which was released on Monday. However, the image was taken nearly a month ago and sources have told ESPN there is little sign of a reconciliation with the club.

Gabriel's representatives believe certain promises made by Man United have also been broken, sources told ESPN.

Gabriel's representatives have been approached by ESPN for comment.

Gabriel, who turns 16 on Tuesday, was due to make his first team debut against Brighton before representatives demanded United cancel his registration over a row about his playing time.

He made his first-team debut in a preseason friendly against Atlético Madrid in the summer, but was omitted from the squad for the Champions League.

Sources have told ESPN that representatives told United he must play at least 20 minutes against Sabah, Brighton and in the Premier League fixture against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Oct. 25 before entering discussions over a scholarship.

Gabriel could have signed a pre-agreement from his 16th birthday on Oct. 6.

With it looking increasingly likely that Gabriel will leave, United, according to sources, are prepared to take legal action if there is evidence of other clubs approaching Gabriel outside of the rules.

They have yet to receive a formal enquiry.

A number of clubs have been linked with a move including Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Despite a breakdown in relations with Gabriel's camp, sources have told ESPN that they continue to believe Old Trafford is the best place for him to develop.

Club officials have made a number of attempts to check on his well-being since he stopped reporting for training.

- Barcelona sporting director: No interest in Man United's JJ Gabriel

- Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United

- Why Man United's wantaway wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

Sources insist they have made every effort to show he has a pathway to the first team, including assigning coaches and specialist staff -- who usually only work with senior players -- to ensure he's prepared for the demands of professional football.

United also accepted a demand from Gabriel to be given the No.77 squad number for this season and petitioned the Premier League on his behalf to allow him to have the name "Gabriel JR" on his shirt.

Sources close to United insist they have prioritised Gabriel's well-being throughout his time at Old Trafford.

There has been a feeling internally that his representatives -- including members of his family -- have been more keen for the forward to break records rather than focus on his long-term development.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.

articles.headline: How a mass Man City player exodus would warp the transfer market
articles.description: If Manchester City are punished by being relegated from the Premier League, group of players worth more than £1 billion in transfer fees would suddenly become available.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ選手の大量流出が移籍市場をどう激変させるか
articles.descriptionJa: もしマンチェスター・シティが罰則としてプレミアリーグから降格することになれば、総額10億ポンド以上の価値がある選手たちが突如として移籍市場に放出されることになる。
articles.body:
What would happen to the transfer market if a group of players worth over £1 billion suddenly became available in the same window, all anxious to immediately find a new club?

If Manchester City fail to overturn an independent commission finding that they were guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period -- City reject the findings and lodged their appeal on Oct. 2 -- the soccer world will find out exactly what it looks like when a collection of superstars and serial winners flood the market.

It would be a football version of "Supermarket Sweep" with Europe's biggest clubs raiding the Etihad Stadium for cut-price deals. With few exceptions, players would be ready to take the first opportunity to escape the crumbling empire they were once so desperate join.

But it would also distort the market more than any previous situation. Chelsea super-charged the transfer market when Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich funded their high spending in the mid-2000s. City took it to another level following Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's takeover in 2008 -- that spending is the root of the problems they now find themselves in with the Premier League. But if the exit doors are forced open at the Etihad, it will drive transfer fees down and change the whole landscape of the market.

With Premier League CEO Richard Masters saying last week that City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade," the likelihood is high of tough sanctions on the club if their appeal fails. Potential punishments include expulsion from the league -- City could be kicked out and forced to apply to rejoin at the bottom of the English football pyramid -- or a huge points deduction that would make relegation to the second-tier Championship unavoidable.

That outcome -- dropping down just one division -- might prove to be the best-case scenario for City. But don't be fooled into believing that the club would be able to ride it out, keep their squad intact and seal an instant return to the top division.

The financial implications of dropping out of the Premier League, and the Champions League, would be seismic even for a club of City's stature and the inevitable outcome would be a mass exodus of their high-earning players.

Championship clubs receive just £5.7 million a year from the EFL's broadcast deal. Last season, City banked £248.9 million in prize money (£165.5 million from the Premier League, £83.4 million from the Champions League), so a hole of more than £240 million would immediately appear in their finances.

City's most recently published wage bill, for the 2024-25 season, amounted to £408.4 million. It is now likely to be closer to an annual £450 million following the arrivals of players including Gianluigi Donnarumma, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández.

articles.headline: Ledley King backs Tottenham form to 'turn around very quickly'
articles.description: Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.
articles.headlineJa: レドリー・キング、トッテナムの調子は「すぐに好転する」と支持
articles.descriptionJa: レドリー・キングは、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームに対し、昨シーズンの経験を活かして、プレミアリーグ新シーズンでの勝ちなしスタートから脱却するよう促した。
articles.body:
Former Tottenham captain Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.

Spurs have been bottom of the table since a 3-2 loss at home to Aston Villa on Sept. 19, which made it two points from five league matches.

After a summer of lavish spending following successive 17th-placed finishes, expectations were raised, but League Cup winner King believes one positive result can act as a catalyst for Tottenham to turn around their form.

The situation was far more bleak for Spurs in March when De Zerbi arrived in north London with the singular focus to avoid a catastrophic relegation to the Championship.

Even though confidence was at an all-time low, De Zerbi masterminded survival after a 15-match winless run in the division was snapped and King believes that experience can help before Saturday's trip to Manchester United.

"It's been tough at the moment, but you can see signs of improvement game by game," King said at a recent Hall of Fame event at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"[They have] no choice. You have to find a way. Most of the group have gone through difficult periods and they managed to find a way out last season.

"They'll have to draw on that to a certain degree, but there is no easy way. You keep working on the training pitch, keep putting the work in.

"It's just a confidence thing. These are top players. I'm sure once the first positive result goes for the team, things can turn around very quickly. Just keep working hard, keep believing in yourself. That's the only way to do it."

- Andrew Robertson after hitting 100 Scotland caps: Hopefully I can catch Kenny Dalglish

- Roberto De Zerbi receives backing of Tottenham's chief executive

- Jan Paul van Hecke returns to Tottenham after suffering foot injury with Netherlands

Former England centre back King spent his entire career at Tottenham and made 323 appearances despite a long-standing knee injury.

King etched his name into club folklore with League Cup success in 2008 and as captain during Spurs' first venture into the Champions League two years later.

After the 45-year-old was one of four people inducted into the relaunched Hall of Fame last month, he received a thunderous reception as a half-time guest for the Villa match.

King said: "To be in the Hall of Fame is really humbling."

articles.headline: Folarin Balogun reopens door to Premier League despite failed Everton move
articles.description: United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.
articles.headlineJa: フォラリン・バログン、エバートンへの移籍失敗後もプレミアリーグ復帰に意欲
articles.descriptionJa: アメリカ代表ストライカーのフォラリン・バログンは、移籍期限最終日にエバートンへの移籍が劇的な形で崩れたものの、依然としてプレミアリーグでのプレーに意欲的であると語った。
articles.body:
United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.

Balogun, 25, backed out of a move to the Toffees after Everton and Monaco started to restructure the terms of his transfer after issues were raised during the his medical examination at Everton's Finch Farm training ground.

Asked by talkSPORT if a Premier League move is something that he'd still be interested in, Balogun said: "Yes, potentially.

"Football has many twists and turns as we've seen after the World Cup.

"I was close to a transfer, didn't materialise, but for sure it's definitely an option."

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said at the time that Balogun abandoned the move due to concerns over his treatment by the Merseyside club.

The former Arsenal forward continues to play his football at Monaco, after a high-profile summer in which he put in some solid performances for the USMNT at the World Cup but also found himself the subject of a major controversy.

Balogun picked up a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the round of 32 and was subsequently banned from the USMNT's round of 16 clash with Belgium.

But then, the red card and ban were overturned by FIFA after U.S. President Donald Trump asked FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to review the decision.

Infantino said the decision was not influenced by Trump. Balogun was handed a suspended ban that allowed him to play against Belgium, but the UMSNT lost and were eliminated from the tournament.

- Folarin Balogun red card U-turn 'most serious incident in the history of football' - LaLiga boss

- Pochettino shares 'regret' over Balogun controversy, impact on USMNT

- David Moyes vents over Everton transfer window after Folarin Balogun deal collapse

Monaco are flying high in Ligue 1 and currently sit at the top of the table after five games, five points ahead of reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain.

Balogun's first match back for Monaco after the summer's transfer debacle was against Lens. Monaco won 2-1.
